findings.description: Structured findings using anchor="file:function" and anchor_line lose their numeric citations. The reducer parses the symbol anchor as citation text, then only considers file/path and line/line_start/start_line; it never consumes anchor_line.
findings.failure_mode: A correctly anchored defect reported exclusively in an adversarial envelope contributes no citation, so review-catch grading reports it as missed and understates recall.
findings.suggested_fix: Support symbol anchors paired with anchor_line and optional anchor_line_end, extracting the file portion of anchor and emitting a normalized numeric citation.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: Refactor gate snapshots run only test_command. The structural check is executed separately for final, but never for implement or fix1 before verdict accuracy is calculated.
findings.failure_mode: For a refactor whose functional tests pass at base, an unchanged fixture snapshot receives accurate=true for APPROVED even though its structural check fails. A gate correctly requesting the missing refactor receives accurate=false.
findings.suggested_fix: Run structural_command(t) on each refactor snapshot and require both functional and structural checks to pass when evaluating that gate's approval.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: parse_pytest applies OUTCOME_RX (`^(PASSED|FAILED|ERROR|XFAIL|XPASS) (\S+)`) to EVERY line of the run output, not only to the 'short test summary info' section. The grader forces `-rA`, which makes pytest print the PASSES section with the captured stdout/stderr (fd-level capture, so subprocess output too) of every passed test, and the FAILURES section prints captured output of failed tests. Any fixture tool under test that prints a line such as `FAILED 2 checks`, `PASSED foo` or `ERROR tests/unit/test_x.py` is parsed as a test outcome: a FAILED/ERROR token becomes a 'bad' node (all_pass false, a spurious t<k> in failed_names), an ERROR token without `::` is treated as a collection error and decrements total (and, if the token is an existing path, expands that file's `def test` functions as failing).
findings.failure_mode: Hidden/regression results are wrong for any task whose fixture emits status words at line start: reference self-check fails or a correct agent tree is graded as failing; conversely total can be under-counted.
findings.suggested_fix: Only scan lines after the `short test summary info` header (or between that header and the final summary line) for OUTCOME_RX; alternatively require the node to contain `::` or end with `.py` and ignore lines inside Captured-output sections.

findings.cross_file_justification: seed-bugfix-tasks.sh / seed-refactor-tasks.sh headers (lines 29-33 and 27-30) state the seeding proof runs `python3 -m pytest` on the host under `env -i PATH HOME LC_ALL` + PYTHONUSERBASE, with no -P/-I; the grader rewrites the same test_command with flags that change sys.path, so a task can prove green at seeding and grade red.
findings.description: Both executors rewrite `python3 -m pytest` with interpreter flags that remove the current directory from sys.path: `-I` (container) implies -P, and `-P` (host) explicitly disables the cwd prepend that `python -m` normally performs. Tests that import fixture modules by top-level package from the tree root (e.g. `from tools.x import y`, common when tests/ has no __init__.py chain pointing at root) raise ModuleNotFoundError under the grader while passing under the seeder's plain `python3 -m pytest` proof and under a developer's shell. Additionally `python3 -P` is only accepted by Python >= 3.11; on a 3.10 host (Ubuntu 22.04) every host-mode pytest invocation exits 2 with 'Unknown option: -P', which run_suite records as parse_error with passed=0 rather than as a tool failure.
findings.failure_mode: Seeded tasks whose tests rely on cwd imports grade 0/N in every arm (visible only when someone runs --self-check reference per task); host mode on Python <3.11 silently grades every build task 0/N with parse_error=true.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep -I/-P for isolation but pass `--rootdir /workspace -o pythonpath=.` (pytest >= 7) or set `-e PYTHONPATH=/workspace` is not possible under -I, so prefer `-p no:cacheprovider --import-mode=importlib` plus `-o pythonpath=.`; make the seeder proof use the identical shaped argv (share shape_command via lib/); detect `Unknown option` / rc 2 with no collected tests as a GradeError instead of a parse_error grade.

findings.description: The outside_path heuristic for Bash takes every ABS_WORD match preceded by whitespace or any of `=:'"\`(<>|;&,` as a filesystem path, exempting only `//…` and one-component `/x/`. Quoted regexes, URL paths and sed/grep patterns are matched: `grep '"/api/v1/users"'`, `sed 's|/old/path|/new|'`, `echo "/a/b"`, `--match '/foo/bar'` all produce candidates like `/api/v1/users` that are outside every allowed root, so the run is marked contaminated (pattern outside_path) on the first such command. Likewise `"hidden" in low` fires on any Grep/WebSearch pattern or file name containing the substring (e.g. `grep -rn hidden src/`, `tests/test_hidden_dirs.py`). The header calls the scan a lower bound, but a false positive is an upper-bound error: it flags a clean run.
findings.failure_mode: Clean runs are reported `contaminated`, and downstream ablation-row.sh/aggregation presumably excludes or penalises them, biasing arm comparisons toward agents that happen not to quote slash-prefixed strings.
findings.suggested_fix: For Bash only treat words that are bare argv tokens (not inside quotes/regex delimiters) or that exist as paths on the allowed/forbidden roots; require a known top-level directory prefix for outside_path (/home, /root, /mnt, /media, /srv, /run, …) rather than 'anything not allowed'; scope the `hidden` check to path-like fields plus Bash words that resolve under the task directory.

findings.description: parse_tap keys tests by their TAP description (`names[n] = desc`), and ids_of later builds `pos = {name: index}`. Bats emits only the `@test` name, not the file, so two tests with the same description in different .bats files (e.g. `"prints usage"`, `"--help exits 0"`) collapse: `bad` is a set of names (one failing copy marks both as bad), `pos` keeps only the last position, so failed_names/newly_failing report the wrong t<k> and lose entries, and `len(order)` still counts both.
findings.failure_mode: For bats-based tasks the per-test ids in hidden_tests.failed_names and regressions.newly_failing are wrong or missing whenever test names repeat across files; counts (passed/total) stay right so the error is silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Key TAP results by test number n (the header already defines TAP ids as the test number): order = list(range(1,total+1)), bad = set of failing numbers, and have ids_of accept integer positions directly.

findings.description: copy_tree(sb, final, EXCLUDE_TOP) copies the whole sandbox except a fixed top-level list and __pycache__/.pytest_cache, and churn() then reads every differing file fully into memory (`open(p,'rb').read()`) and runs difflib on it. Nothing excludes agent-created dependency or build trees (.venv, node_modules, .tox, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, dist/, coverage files, large logs). A single `pip install -e .`/`npm install` during the agent run adds tens of thousands of files that are (a) copied into grading/final, (b) each counted in files_changed and, when text, in diff_lines, and (c) read whole into memory; a large binary/log the agent left behind can exhaust memory and abort the grade with exit 2.
findings.failure_mode: diff_lines/files_changed, which are compared across arms as churn metrics, are dominated by installed dependencies rather than the agent's edits; grading time and disk use scale with the agent's environment, and a multi-GB artefact aborts grading (MemoryError → internal error exit 2).
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the exclusion set with common dependency/build/cache directories (.venv, venv, node_modules, .tox, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .eggs, *.egg-info, dist, build) or honour the sandbox .gitignore; in churn, skip files above a size cap (e.g. 2 MiB) and count them as 1 file/0 lines; stream hashes instead of reading both sides fully.

findings.description: envelope_texts collects `anchor` verbatim and, separately, `file`/`path` + `line`/`line_start`/`start_line`. The dissent envelope schema in use for adversarial review/audit (the same schema this reviewer emits: `anchor: "file:symbol"`, `anchor_line`, `anchor_line_end`, `anchor_type`) has neither a `file` nor a `line` key, and its `anchor` is `file:symbol`, which the CITE regex does not match (it requires `:digits`). Consequently no dissent finding of the form {anchor: 'evals/x.sh:fn', anchor_line: 120} ever becomes a `path:line` citation in gates-combined.md, so recall never credits the adversarial gate and false_positives ignore it, contrary to the header's 'each finding's anchor (and file:line) in eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json'.
findings.failure_mode: review-catch recall under-counts (defects caught only by the dissent reviewer are reported as missed), silently skewing the DEC-0420 arm comparison for arms where the adversarial gate is the one that catches the defect.
findings.suggested_fix: When `anchor_line` is an int, split `anchor` on the first ':' to get the file and emit `f"{file}:{anchor_line}"` (or `{anchor_line}-{anchor_line_end}`); also accept `anchor` strings already in `path:line` form as today.

findings.description: When the final-tree regression run has no parseable summary, newly_failing is set to every base-passing test regardless of the exit code. run_suite's parse_error branch, however, credits passed=total when rc==0. So for a final tree whose regression command exits 0 but prints an unparseable summary (e.g. the agent added a `-qq`/`-p no:terminal` to pytest.ini, or switched a bats formatter), grade.json reports regressions.final.passed == regressions.final.total alongside newly_failing listing every test.
findings.failure_mode: Self-contradictory regressions block in grade.json; aggregation that uses newly_failing counts the run as a total regression while the counts say green, and the opposite choice is equally unjustified.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the two consistent: if rf.parse_error, set newly_failing = base_ok only when rf.rc != 0, else [] and surface `parse_error: true` inside the regressions object so consumers can see the uncertainty.
